original_limitation: Smoking promotes atherosclerosis but is not the sole cause. The source does not establish that every smoker develops clinically significant plaque or quantify individual plaque progression.

original_verified_claim: Atherosclerotic plaque accumulation in the coronary arteries is the leading cause of coronary heart disease, also known as coronary artery disease. Plaque causes coronary arteries to harden and narrow, potentially reducing or blocking blood flow to the heart muscle.
original_limitation: Coronary plaque buildup is the leading cause of coronary heart disease but not its only mechanism. Coronary microvascular dysfunction and vasospasm can also contribute. The presence of plaque does not necessarily indicate symptomatic disease.

original_passage_locator: Table 1 → Pulmonary impairment after TB; PIAT → Epidemiology; Variability in lung function deficits; Airflow obstruction; Restrictive ventilatory defects
original_verified_claim: The review reports persistent obstructive and restrictive lung-function abnormalities after pulmonary TB and describes associations between structural damage and impairment. Cavities are associated with lower FEV1, bronchiectasis with airflow obstruction, and extensive fibrosis is proposed as an explanation for restrictive ventilatory defects. The authors describe structural remodeling as a probable contributor to post-TB impairment.
original_limitation: Although physiologically plausible mechanisms are discussed, the review does not establish that residual structural damage independently causes later impairment in all cases. Much of the epidemiological evidence is observational, baseline lung function is often unavailable, and the authors acknowledge incomplete understanding of the causal mechanisms. The relation is therefore recorded as ASSOCIATED_WITH rather than a confirmed CAUSES arrow.
original_review_note: Reviewed Ravimohan et al., particularly Table 1, Variability in lung function deficits, Airflow obstruction and Restrictive ventilatory defects. The article connects cavitation, fibrosis, bronchiectasis and lung remodeling with persistent pulmonary dysfunction, but frequently describes the proposed mechanisms as probable or possible. The structural injury-to-impairment relationship is supported as an association; independent causality is not conclusively established. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.

original_passage_locator: Unstructured summary; The burden of PTLD; Causal pathways underlying PTLD; Heterogeneity of PTLD; Table 1 → Observed patterns of TB-related lung damage
original_verified_claim: Meghji et al. describe post-tuberculosis lung disease as encompassing residual parenchymal and airway abnormalities, including fibrosis, cavitation and bronchiectasis, alongside persistent respiratory symptoms and impaired lung function. The review reports ongoing abnormalities after completion of TB treatment and recognizes an association between residual structural pathology and post-TB respiratory limitation.
original_limitation: The review explicitly states that causal pathways underlying PTLD remain poorly understood. Structural abnormalities, lung-function impairment and symptoms vary considerably and do not always correlate closely. Smoking, environmental exposures, comorbidities, deconditioning and other factors may contribute to impairment. The source supports association rather than an independently established causal effect of scarring on persistent respiratory limitation.
original_review_note: Reviewed the supplied Meghji et al. Post-tuberculosis lung disease: Towards prevention, diagnosis and care, particularly the Unstructured summary, The burden of PTLD, Causal pathways underlying PTLD, Heterogeneity of PTLD and Table 1. The review documents residual structural abnormalities and persistent respiratory limitations in TB survivors but emphasizes incomplete causal understanding. Supports Lung tissue injury and scarring → Persistent respiratory limitation after tuberculosis as ASSOCIATED_WITH, not confirmed CAUSES. AI-assisted review; human confirmation pending.
